author: Mark Atwood
text:
/do-beads JMAP-wzq9 invoked at 2026-05-14. The epic has 6 ready beads (wzq9.29, .30, .31, .32, .33, .34), but every one of them has body text or sibling structure (parent .15/.20 blocked-by tjvm.16; .3 blocked-by tjvm.5) that says the fix must propagate from canonical jmap-mail-client first per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule.

The agent cannot close any of the 6 ready beads without either:

(A) Expanding scope outside the stated epic (touch crate-jmap-mail-client first, then propagate to all 7 extension-client siblings, then close wzq9 beads as part of a workspace-wide sweep). This violates AGENTS.md 'Scope and Style' ('only touch files within the task's stated scope... if a fix requires changes outside scope, stop and ask').

(B) Add blocked-by deps from the relevant canonical tjvm beads to these 6 wzq9 beads (mirroring the discipline already on .15/.20/.3), file 3 new tjvm beads for the canonical patterns not yet tracked there (hand-rolled props serde at tjvm-mail-client, missing # Errors rustdoc family-wide, with_<ext>_session deferred-validation contract family-wide), and exit with empty ready frontier on this epic. This is curation-only work; no code changes.

(C) Violate the canonical-first rule by fixing metadata-client first (upward divergence). The rule reads as rigid in AGENTS.md.

Recommendation: (B). The curation is genuinely missing — the 'extends wzq9.15/.20/.21' beads inherited the parent's scope but not its canonical-first blocker.

Per AGENTS.md 'Turn questions into beads' rule and the 'do not file human on obvious-thing-recommendations' caveat: this IS a recommendation, but the underlying call is a scope-decision the human owns: did the /do-beads invocation actually mean 'descendants of JMAP-wzq9 only' (in which case path B is correct), or 'metadata-client review findings, however far the propagation has to reach' (in which case path A is correct)? Filing as human-labeled so the next reviewer makes the call.

No code changes made. Ready frontier under JMAP-wzq9 is preserved.
